units.section_heading: The strange alarm hidden in a kitchen staple
units.exact_text: An onion can sit quietly on a counter for days and do nothing to your eyes.

units.section_heading: The strange alarm hidden in a kitchen staple
units.exact_text: Cut it open, and within seconds the same vegetable can make you blink, sting, and tear up.

units.section_heading: The strange alarm hidden in a kitchen staple
units.exact_text: That feels almost absurd.

units.section_heading: The strange alarm hidden in a kitchen staple
units.exact_text: Nothing has been heated, burned, or sprayed.

units.section_heading: The strange alarm hidden in a kitchen staple
units.exact_text: You simply broke a few layers of plant tissue.

units.section_heading: The strange alarm hidden in a kitchen staple
units.exact_text: But that damage is exactly the point.

units.section_heading: The strange alarm hidden in a kitchen staple
units.exact_text: An onion does not store its irritating chemistry as one ready-made gas waiting to escape.

units.section_heading: The strange alarm hidden in a kitchen staple
units.exact_text: It stores separate ingredients inside living cells, and cutting lets those ingredients meet.

units.section_heading: The strange alarm hidden in a kitchen staple
units.exact_text: What happens next is a tiny chemical chain reaction built into the plant.

units.section_heading: The strange alarm hidden in a kitchen staple
units.exact_text: And the tears are not an emotional response at all.

units.section_heading: The strange alarm hidden in a kitchen staple
units.exact_text: They are a protective reflex from your eyes.

units.section_heading: The onion keeps the ingredients apart
units.exact_text: Inside an intact onion, sulfur-containing precursor compounds and an enzyme called alliinase are kept in different parts of the cells.

units.section_heading: The onion keeps the ingredients apart
units.exact_text: Alliinase is simply a protein that speeds up a chemical reaction.

units.section_heading: The onion keeps the ingredients apart
units.exact_text: As long as the cells stay intact, the ingredients are largely separated.

units.section_heading: The onion keeps the ingredients apart
units.exact_text: A knife changes that arrangement instantly.

units.section_heading: The onion keeps the ingredients apart
units.exact_text: When the blade breaks cell walls and membranes, compounds that were stored apart spill into the same damaged tissue.

units.section_heading: The onion keeps the ingredients apart
units.exact_text: Alliinase can now act on the sulfur-containing precursors.

units.section_heading: The onion keeps the ingredients apart
units.exact_text: That reaction produces unstable sulfur compounds called sulfenic acids.

units.section_heading: The onion keeps the ingredients apart
units.exact_text: They do not remain in that form for long.

units.section_heading: The onion keeps the ingredients apart
units.exact_text: They are reactive intermediates, temporary molecules created on the way to other products.

units.section_heading: The onion keeps the ingredients apart
units.exact_text: This is why chopping an onion changes its smell almost immediately.

units.section_heading: The onion keeps the ingredients apart
units.exact_text: The odor is not just something that was trapped inside the bulb.

units.section_heading: The onion keeps the ingredients apart
units.exact_text: Part of it is being manufactured at the moment the tissue is damaged.

units.section_heading: The enzyme scientists did not expect
units.exact_text: For years, researchers thought the tear-causing molecule formed more or less automatically after alliinase began the reaction.

units.section_heading: The enzyme scientists did not expect
units.exact_text: Then a 2002 Nature paper changed the picture.

units.section_heading: The enzyme scientists did not expect
units.exact_text: The researchers showed that onions use another enzyme, lachrymatory-factor synthase, to specifically make the tear-causing factor.

units.section_heading: The enzyme scientists did not expect
units.exact_text: The name sounds intimidating, but its job is simple: it helps turn a short-lived sulfur intermediate into the molecule that makes your eyes water.

units.section_heading: The enzyme scientists did not expect
units.exact_text: That finding matters because the onion is not merely releasing a random irritating by-product.

units.section_heading: The enzyme scientists did not expect
units.exact_text: It has a dedicated biochemical step that produces it.

units.section_heading: The enzyme scientists did not expect
units.exact_text: Later structural and biochemical work examined how this enzyme performs that conversion.

units.section_heading: The enzyme scientists did not expect
units.exact_text: The chemistry is fast enough that, from a cook's point of view, it seems instantaneous.

units.section_heading: The enzyme scientists did not expect
units.exact_text: Slice, and the reaction begins.

units.section_heading: The molecule that reaches your eyes
units.exact_text: The main tear-causing compound is syn-propanethial S-oxide, a small volatile sulfur compound often called the onion lachrymatory factor.

units.section_heading: The molecule that reaches your eyes
units.exact_text: Volatile means it can readily enter the air.

units.section_heading: The molecule that reaches your eyes
units.exact_text: Once it forms in the damaged onion, some of it moves away from the cutting board and reaches the moist surface of your eyes.

units.section_heading: The molecule that reaches your eyes
units.exact_text: There it acts as an irritant.

units.section_heading: The molecule that reaches your eyes
units.exact_text: Your eye does not need to know that the molecule came from a vegetable.

units.section_heading: The molecule that reaches your eyes
units.exact_text: It only needs to detect that the surface is being chemically irritated.

units.section_heading: The molecule that reaches your eyes
units.exact_text: That triggers reflex tears, the protective tears produced when dust, smoke, or another irritant reaches the eye.

units.section_heading: The molecule that reaches your eyes
units.exact_text: The extra fluid helps dilute and wash away the irritating material.

units.section_heading: The molecule that reaches your eyes
units.exact_text: So the stream running down your face is not the onion somehow forcing emotion out of you.

units.section_heading: The molecule that reaches your eyes
units.exact_text: It is your eye performing a cleanup response.

units.section_heading: Why onions evolved such chemistry
units.exact_text: The reaction makes more sense when we stop thinking like cooks and start thinking like plants.

units.section_heading: Why onions evolved such chemistry
units.exact_text: An onion cannot run away when something bites into it.

units.section_heading: Why onions evolved such chemistry
units.exact_text: Chemical defense is one of the tools available to a plant that is rooted in place.

units.section_heading: Why onions evolved such chemistry
units.exact_text: Researchers studying onion chemistry describe the sulfur pathway as part of a broader defense system against microbes and animals.

units.section_heading: Why onions evolved such chemistry
units.exact_text: Damage activates a burst of reactive sulfur chemistry.

units.section_heading: Why onions evolved such chemistry
units.exact_text: Some of the products contribute to the sharp smell and flavor we associate with onions.

units.section_heading: Why onions evolved such chemistry
units.exact_text: One branch of that chemistry produces the lachrymatory factor.

units.section_heading: Why onions evolved such chemistry
units.exact_text: From the plant's perspective, tissue damage is a moment when chemical defense is useful.

units.section_heading: Why onions evolved such chemistry
units.exact_text: From our perspective, it is the moment dinner becomes uncomfortable.

units.section_heading: Why onions evolved such chemistry
units.exact_text: The same chemistry can therefore be both biologically useful to the plant and culinarily annoying to us.

units.section_heading: Why some cuts feel worse than others
units.exact_text: The amount of irritation you experience can vary because several things change how much reactive chemistry is created and how much of the volatile product reaches your face.

units.section_heading: Why some cuts feel worse than others
units.exact_text: More tissue damage means more cell contents can mix.

units.section_heading: Why some cuts feel worse than others
units.exact_text: Air movement matters because the tear factor has to travel from the onion to your eyes.

units.section_heading: Why some cuts feel worse than others
units.exact_text: The onion itself also matters.

units.section_heading: Why some cuts feel worse than others
units.exact_text: Different onions do not contain identical amounts of the precursor compounds or produce identical levels of pungent sulfur chemistry.

units.section_heading: Why some cuts feel worse than others
units.exact_text: And people differ in how strongly they react to irritants.

units.section_heading: Why some cuts feel worse than others
units.exact_text: That is why two people can chop the same onion and report very different experiences.

units.section_heading: Why some cuts feel worse than others
units.exact_text: The underlying pathway can be the same even when the subjective intensity is not.

units.section_heading: Can an onion be made that does not make you cry?
units.exact_text: Yes, at least in experimental lines, researchers have shown that the pathway can be redirected.

units.section_heading: Can an onion be made that does not make you cry?
units.exact_text: Studies that suppressed the activity of lachrymatory-factor synthase produced onions with dramatically reduced tear-factor formation.

units.section_heading: Can an onion be made that does not make you cry?
units.exact_text: When that enzyme is less active, the sulfur intermediate is available for other reactions instead of being efficiently converted into the lachrymatory factor.

units.section_heading: Can an onion be made that does not make you cry?
units.exact_text: That result is useful for two reasons.

units.section_heading: Can an onion be made that does not make you cry?
units.exact_text: First, it confirms that the tear-producing enzyme really is a key control point in the pathway.

units.section_heading: Can an onion be made that does not make you cry?
units.exact_text: Second, it shows that reducing tears does not require removing all sulfur chemistry from the onion.

units.section_heading: Can an onion be made that does not make you cry?
units.exact_text: The plant's chemistry can be shifted rather than simply switched off.

units.section_heading: Can an onion be made that does not make you cry?
units.exact_text: Breeding and biotechnology can therefore change how strongly an onion activates this particular defense branch.

units.section_heading: What actually helps in the kitchen
units.exact_text: Once you understand the mechanism, many kitchen tricks become easier to judge.

units.section_heading: What actually helps in the kitchen
units.exact_text: The tear factor has to be produced in damaged tissue and then reach your eyes through the air.

units.section_heading: What actually helps in the kitchen
units.exact_text: So the most direct strategy is to reduce your exposure to the airborne irritant.

units.section_heading: What actually helps in the kitchen
units.exact_text: Moving air away from your face with good ventilation can help carry the volatile compound elsewhere.

units.section_heading: What actually helps in the kitchen
units.exact_text: A very sharp knife can also reduce unnecessary crushing compared with a badly blunted blade, although cutting still damages cells and cannot stop the chemistry completely.

units.section_heading: What actually helps in the kitchen
units.exact_text: Anything that places your eyes farther from the rising vapor can reduce exposure simply by changing where the air goes.

units.section_heading: What actually helps in the kitchen
units.exact_text: The important point is that no trick needs to "neutralize emotion" or pull toxins out of the onion.

units.section_heading: What actually helps in the kitchen
units.exact_text: This is ordinary plant chemistry meeting ordinary eye protection.

units.section_heading: The whole chain in one cut
units.exact_text: So why do onions make us cry?

units.section_heading: The whole chain in one cut
units.exact_text: Because a knife turns separated cellular ingredients into a rapid chemical assembly line.

units.section_heading: The whole chain in one cut
units.exact_text: Cell damage brings sulfur precursors together with alliinase.

units.section_heading: The whole chain in one cut
units.exact_text: Alliinase creates short-lived sulfur intermediates.

units.section_heading: The whole chain in one cut
units.exact_text: Lachrymatory-factor synthase redirects one of those intermediates toward syn-propanethial S-oxide.

units.section_heading: The whole chain in one cut
units.exact_text: That volatile molecule reaches the eye and irritates its surface.

units.section_heading: The whole chain in one cut
units.exact_text: The eye answers with reflex tears that dilute and wash away the irritant.

units.section_heading: The whole chain in one cut
units.exact_text: The remarkable part is how much biology is compressed into those few seconds.

units.section_heading: The whole chain in one cut
units.exact_text: What looks like a simple nuisance in the kitchen is actually a defense system, an enzyme pathway, an airborne chemical signal, and a protective human reflex unfolding one after another.

units.section_heading: The whole chain in one cut
units.exact_text: An onion does not contain a tiny bottle of tear gas.

units.section_heading: The whole chain in one cut
units.exact_text: It contains the machinery to make an irritant when its tissue is damaged.

units.section_heading: The whole chain in one cut
units.exact_text: Your knife starts the chemistry.

units.section_heading: The whole chain in one cut
units.exact_text: Your eyes finish the story.
